refined_question: Let X be a Banach space and let (T(t))_{t\ge 0} be a C0-semigroup on X. Define its growth bound by ω0(T) := inf{ω \in \mathbb{R} : there exists a constant M_ω > 0 such that ||T(t)|| \le M_ω e^{\omega t} for all t \ge 0}. Find conditions on (T(t))_{t\ge 0} under which this infimum is attained; equivalently, characterize when there exists a constant M0 > 0 such that ||T(t)|| \le M0 e^{\omega0(T) t} for every t \ge 0.
equivalent_formulation: Characterize those C0-semigroups for which the infimum in the definition of the growth bound ω0(T) is a minimum.
justification: The draft is targeting the exact statement of Section 3, Problem 14, not the neighboring Problem 13. The paper states essentially the same question, with the same growth-bound formula and the same request to determine when ω0 is a minimum. The only nearby contextual addition is the comment that this amounts to a characterization of boundedness for semigroups. Since the paper does not impose extra hypotheses here, the faithful refinement is to make the Banach-space setting, strong continuity, operator norm, and the existential role of M_ω explicit, while avoiding any extra assumptions not present in the paper.
